tools.name: broadcast_message
tools.title: Broadcast Message
tools.description: Sends a message through the project's connector to a segment of its members. DESTRUCTIVE AND IRREVERSIBLE: you MUST show a human the exact message text, the audience segment and the recipient count from `preview_broadcast_audience`, and get explicit approval, before calling. A broadcast cannot be recalled once queued and every recipient is a real person. NOT idempotent — calling twice sends twice. Emits `broadcast.queued` then `broadcast.completed` with sent/failed tallies. Use `preview_broadcast_audience` first, always. Answers with `broadcast_id`: the creator follows the send on the dashboard and in the Copilot, and `get_broadcast` reads its tallies and the members it could not reach.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose members will receive the message.

message.description: The message body, 1-4096 characters. Canonical HTML subset only (<b>, <i>, <u>, <s>, <a>, <code>, <pre>, <blockquote>, <tg-spoiler>); anything else is stripped before sending.

audience.description: Segment to address: all, customer, trialing, lead, churned, expiring_soon, cancelled_still_active, paused, trialing_cardless, waiting_on_connection, all_pass_holders, all_pass_holders_not_in_queue, pass_holders, pass_holders_not_in_queue. Defaults to `all`, which reaches every member with a linked chat.

pass_window_id.description: Required for the single-window pass segments (`pass_holders`, `pass_holders_not_in_queue`); ignored by the others.

plan_id.description: Optional. Narrows the segment to members on one subscription plan, by plan UUID. Composes with the segment rather than replacing it: `customer` plus a plan reaches people paying for that plan right now, `churned` plus a plan reaches people who held it and left. Rejected for `lead` (never subscribed) and for the pass segments (their plan is implied by the window).

expiring_within_days.description: Only meaningful for `expiring_soon`. How many days ahead to look, 1-90, default 7. A member is counted only if their access genuinely lapses: an auto-renewing subscription is not expiring.

tools.name: cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel Subscription
tools.description: Cancels a subscription. Async — the call queues a provider-side cancellation; the local row flips to `canceled` and `subscription.cancelled` emits when the worker finishes. Returns `{ subscription_id, status: "cancellation_queued" }` immediately. DESTRUCTIVE: you MUST confirm the target `subscription_id` with a human before calling — this stops billing and revokes connector resource access on the next sync. Idempotent — already-canceled subscriptions return `SUBSCRIPTION_ALREADY_ACTIVE` rather than double-firing.

subscription_id.description: UUID of the subscription to cancel.

tools.name: get_dashboard_metrics
tools.title: Headline Dashboard Metrics
tools.description: Returns headline dashboard metrics for the authenticated creator: MRR, active subscribers, churn, and a plan-level breakdown, with a comparison-window delta. Accepts a `period` preset (`7d`, `14d`, `30d`, `60d`, `90d`, `mtd`, `qtd`, `ytd`, `1y`, `all`) or explicit `from`/`to` ISO dates. Pair with `get_earnings_report` for the timeseries view and `get_subscriber_analytics` for lifecycle detail. Backed by the same 5-minute cache the dashboard uses, so repeated calls within a window return the same numbers.

project_id.description: Optional project UUID to scope the metrics to. Leave blank for all projects in the current team.

period.description: Period preset — 7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 90d, mtd, qtd, ytd, 1y, all. Defaults to 30d. Ignored when both from and to are supplied.

from.description: Explicit start date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Overrides period when paired with "to".

to.description: Explicit end date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Overrides period when paired with "from".

compare_period.description: Baseline to compare against — "previous" (prior window) or "none". Defaults to "previous".

tools.name: get_me
tools.title: Get Me
tools.description: Describes the creator this token belongs to: id, name, email, locale, platform plan and its capabilities, the team the token is scoped to (`current_team`, the id the other tools act in) and every team they belong to, the accounts linked on the connectors, and where their alerts go (`alert_destinations`, with `alert_destinations_default` true when no destination was written and every class reaches the primary connected account). Call it first to learn who you are acting as. Takes no input.

tools.name: get_portal_design
tools.title: Get Portal Design
tools.description: Reads a project's portal design: `published`, the document members see, and `draft`, the one being edited or null, each with every key of the fourteen sections (colours, typography, shape, layout, wording, blocks, button and footer, announcement bar, media, sections, behaviour, visibility and code, language) in the stored shape `update_portal_design` takes back, plus `has_draft`, `draft_updated_at`, `published_at` and a preview_url that shows the draft for ten minutes, null until the project has a handle. Requires `project_id`. Unknown or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose portal design to read.

tools.name: get_project
tools.title: Get Project
tools.description: Fetches a single project by UUID, including counts of `plans`, `resources`, `subscribers`, and `payment_methods`. TenantScope enforces that the project belongs to the caller's team — unknown or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (no existence leaks). Pair with `list_projects` to discover the right id first.

project_id.description: UUID of the project to fetch.

tools.name: get_recovery_readiness
tools.title: Get Recovery Readiness
tools.description: Reads the Disaster Recovery readiness checklist for the creator this token acts for: every line (the account lines first: a second factor and a backup sign-in account; then each installed connector's own lines, named by `connector`, such as a standby installation, a standby for every gated space, automatic failover and a live mirror; then the reminders: a copy of the content kept elsewhere and a second human administrator) with `done` true, false, or null when the platform can only remind, `locked` when the plan lacks the prevention feature, the state in words (`detail`) and where the fix lives (`url`), plus the totals the dashboard card shows (`completed` of `total`, `complete`, and `prevention` for whether the plan bundles the prevention features). Answers "how ready is this account for the next ban?". Takes no input.

tools.name: list_connector_installations
tools.title: List Connector Installations
tools.description: The health of the connectors on a project: the connection state of each bot or app and whether it can act right now. Lists every connector installation a project holds, oldest first: the `connector` key, the `scope` (`project`, or `platform` for a shared presence Subscriby runs), the `role` (`live` or `standby`), the `state` (`pending`, `connected`, `degraded`, `revoked`, `disconnected`) with its `state_reason` and `state_detail`, whether the creator can fix it (`creator_actionable`), whether it can act right now (`operational`), the platform's own `external_id`, `display_name`, `handle` and `avatar_url`, and when it was connected, verified, revoked, disconnected or uninstalled. Credentials and settings never appear. Answers "which connectors does this project run, and are they healthy?".

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose installations to list.

tools.name: list_payment_methods
tools.title: List Payment Methods
tools.description: Lists configured payment methods for one project. Provider secrets, webhook signing secrets, and Stripe Connect account ids are always stripped — only `id`, `provider`, `connector`, `mode`, `active`, and `created_at` are surfaced. `provider` is a gateway code or a `connector:provider` key for a currency a connector brings, and `connector` names that connector or is null. Set `active_only=true` to omit deactivated methods. Safe to call when deciding whether a plan can charge against a given provider.

project_id.description: UUID of the project whose payment methods to list.

active_only.description: When true, omits deactivated payment methods.

tools.name: list_plans
tools.title: List Plans
tools.description: Lists subscription plans, optionally narrowed to one project via `project_id`. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page` (default 1). Every row carries a `kind` — subscription, pass or pass_series — and that kind names the ONE nested block accompanying it: `billing` (cycle, trial, renewal), `pass` (timezone, recurrence, sales cutoff, next sellable window) or `pass_series` (span, window count, seats, successor). The other two are absent, so a billing cycle never appears on a plan where the cycle means nothing. Every row also carries `cadence`, the human-readable duration string the portal and bot show. Use to discover plan ids before calling `get_plan_performance`, `list_access_codes`, `bulk_generate_access_codes`, `cancel_subscription`, or `list_pass_windows`.

project_id.description: Optional project UUID to narrow the list to a single project.

limit.description: Maximum plans to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_projects
tools.title: List Projects
tools.description: Lists every project the token's frozen team can access, ordered by `created_at` descending. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page` (default 1). The starting point for most flows — use to discover project ids before calling any other tool that takes a `project_id`.

limit.description: Maximum projects to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_resources
tools.title: List Resources
tools.description: Lists resources attached to one project (the places a connector gates, plus manual perks) ordered by `created_at` descending. Paginates with `limit` (1..100, default 25) and `page`; narrows with `kind` (`manual`, or a connector's kind spelled `connector:kind` as `list_connectors` lists each connector's `resource_kinds`) and `connector` (a connector key). Each row carries `kind`, `connector` (null for a manual perk) and `space` (`{id, external_id, title}` when linked, `null` for a perk or an unlinked placeholder). Use to discover resource ids before calling `get_resource`, `unlink_resource`, or `delete_resource`.

limit.description: Maximum resources to return per page (1..100).

kind.description: Only resources of one kind: `manual`, or a connector's kind spelled `connector:kind` as `list_connectors` lists each connector's `resource_kinds`.

connector.description: Only the resources one connector gates, by the key `list_connectors` lists it under.

tools.name: list_subscribers
tools.title: List Subscribers
tools.description: Lists project members (subscribers) with optional filters: `project_id`, `status` (`lead`, `trialing`, `customer`, `churned`, `banned`), `access` (`waiting`: members whose live purchase includes a place waiting for an account they have not connected, the ones `remind_member_to_connect` nudges), and `search` (case-insensitive partial match across name, email and billing email). Paginates with `limit` (1..100) and `page`. Returns both `email` (member-chosen, verified, their portal sign-in credential) and `billing_email` (whatever they gave a payment provider, never verified — identification only, not a contact channel). PII WARNING: both are returned verbatim — scrub before forwarding to any third-party LLM, log sink, or analytics surface.

project_id.description: Optional project UUID to narrow the result.

status.description: Member status filter. One of: lead, trialing, customer, churned, banned

access.description: `waiting` keeps the members whose live purchase includes a place waiting for an account they have not connected; omit for everyone.

search.description: Case-insensitive partial match against name + email.

limit.description: Maximum members to return per page (1..100).

tools.name: list_teams
tools.title: List Teams
tools.description: Lists every team the authenticated user owns or holds a membership in. Each row carries `personal` so the personal team is identifiable. Useful before minting a token scoped to a specific team via the dashboard. Team CRUD stays dashboard-only — no `create_team` / `delete_team` tools exist.

tools.name: list_webhook_endpoints
tools.title: List Webhook Endpoints
tools.description: Lists outbound webhook endpoints registered for the token's team. Optionally scoped by `project_id`, or trimmed by `active_only` to hide endpoints with `is_active=false` or `disabled_at` set. Webhook signing secrets are NEVER returned; only `url`, the `events` allow-list, `failure_count`, `consecutive_failures`, and `last_success_at` / `last_failure_at` timestamps. Cross-reference allowed `events` against `subscriby://enums/webhook-event` to confirm coverage.

project_id.description: Optional project UUID. Omit to list team-wide endpoints and all project-scoped endpoints within the team.

active_only.description: When true, hides endpoints with is_active=false or disabled_at set.

tools.name: preview_broadcast_audience
tools.title: Preview Broadcast Audience
tools.description: Sizes a broadcast without sending anything. Returns every audience segment this project can address with its current recipient count and the estimated send duration. Call this BEFORE `broadcast_message` and show the human the count — a segment that silently resolves to every member is the one mistake a broadcast cannot be taken back from. Omit `audience` to list all segments.

project_id.description: UUID of the project to size a broadcast for.

audience.description: Size one segment only. Omit to receive every segment with its count.

pass_window_id.description: Needed to size the single-window pass segments; without it they report a null count.

plan_id.description: Optional plan UUID. Sizes each segment as narrowed to that plan. Segments that cannot use a plan filter (`lead`, the pass segments) report their unnarrowed count and a null plan_id.

expiring_within_days.description: How far ahead `expiring_soon` looks, 1-90, default 7. Ignored by every other segment.

tools.name: get_subscription
tools.title: Get Subscription
tools.description: Fetches one subscription by UUID: its plan, subscriber, payment method, payment status, price, trial end, end date, whether it was cancelled, when an access code was redeemed, and its access `grants` (one per resource and pass window, with connector, mode, state and failure). The same fields the REST subscription payload carries. Use before `cancel_subscription`, `pause_subscription` or `remind_pass_holder` to read the current state back rather than assuming it. Unknown, foreign or out-of-scope ids surface as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.

subscription_id.description: UUID of the subscription to fetch.

tools.name: list_broadcast_audiences
tools.title: List Broadcast Audiences
tools.description: Lists every audience segment `broadcast_message` accepts for a project: the segment's value and label, what it means, whether it requires a pass window, whether it can be narrowed to a plan, whether it reads the expiring-within-days horizon, and a recipient estimate (null for segments that need a pass window first). Call it before composing a broadcast; `preview_broadcast_audience` sizes one segment with your exact filters. Requires `project_id`.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the broadcast would go to.

tools.name: list_subscriptions
tools.title: List Subscriptions
tools.description: Pages every subscription the token may see, newest first: id, plan, subscriber, payment method, payment status, price, trial end, end date and whether it was cancelled — the same row shape `get_subscription` answers, which adds the access grants. Optional "status" matches one payment status ("trialing", "active", "incomplete", "expired", "past_due", "canceled", "unpaid", "paused", "processing", "succeeded", "capturable" or "failed"; an unknown word is `VALIDATION_FAILED`), "plan_id" scopes to one plan, and `limit` (1..100, default 25) with `page` walk the pages. `list_subscribers` lists the people; this lists their purchases.

status.description: Match one payment status word; an unknown value is refused naming the accepted list.

plan_id.description: Scope to one plan by UUID.
